equations: Fatigue life = N_f = A * (Δσ)^(-b)
where A is material constant, Δσ is stress range, b is fatigue exponent
accepted.boundary_conditions: Effective for components experiencing cyclic loading; less effective for impact-dominated loading
accepted.cross_domain_transition: Manufacturing stress-resistant coatings -> automotive suspension component protection (extends component lifetime under cyclic loading)

baseline.baseline_incumbent: Traditional thermal spray coatings without stress optimization
baseline.baseline_metric: Standard coatings show 10^5 cycles to failure in fatigue testing
baseline.candidate_metric: 1.5-2.0 × 10^5 cycles to failure in fatigue testing

killer_experiment.experiment: Fatigue testing with controlled stress cycling, optimized HVOF vs. standard coatings, cycles to failure measurement, n=20 samples
killer_experiment.decisive_uncertainty: Optimal coating thickness for different stress conditions
killer_experiment.kill_condition: Coating delamination occurs before 5 × 10^4 cycles or 20% reduction in fatigue strength

commercial_path.use_case: Protection of suspension components, brake systems, and other stressed automotive parts
commercial_path.integration_point: Applied as protective coating on critical automotive components during manufacturing

medical_screen.basis: no medical-application vocabulary in the target application fields
